LESSON: SELF- AWARENESS

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: question(s) Creation
Topic 1.1: Self- Awareness

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Self- Awareness. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: what they like about special before a) state what they like about themselves God?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Self- Awareness means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Self- Awareness from Kenya
3. practise Self- Awareness in clear steps
4. apply Self- Awareness in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SELF- AWARENESS
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Self- Awareness helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: SELF- AWARENESS
Study Self- Awareness like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Self- Awareness means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Self- Awareness means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Self- Awareness means in simple pupil language.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Self- Awareness” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Self- Awareness means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Self- Awareness from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Self- Awareness from Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Self- Awareness from Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Self- Awareness in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Self- Awareness from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Self- Awareness in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Self- Awareness in clear steps. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Self- Awareness in clear steps.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Self- Awareness in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Self- Awareness in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Self- Awareness in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Self- Awareness in one real-life situation this week.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Self- Awareness” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Self- Awareness in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Self- Awareness is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Self- Awareness” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain what Self- Awareness means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Self- Awareness in your own words. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Self- Awareness from Kenya)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: practise Self- Awareness in clear steps)

Example 4: Show how “Self- Awareness” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: apply Self- Awareness in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Self- Awareness to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Self- Awareness means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Self- Awareness from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Self- Awareness in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Self- Awareness from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Self- Awareness: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Self- Awareness?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. what they like about special before a) state what they like about themselves God?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Self- Awareness means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Self- Awareness means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Self- Awareness from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
